relations.rationale: Nervousness before presenting has no bearing on the later cleanup activity.
A brief wave between two individuals doesn't establish or affect the general excitement level of the gymnasium.
A buzzing, excited crowd moving table to table suggests visitors were engaged and likely appreciating the projects, supporting the idea they admired the creativity.
The general excitement of the fair doesn't specifically indicate anything about how Zeno perceived the duration of his shift.
The fair being busy in early afternoon doesn't directly relate to what happens later when it winds down and people pack up.
Visitors admiring projects doesn't have a direct causal or evidential link to the act of packing up afterward.
Zeno's shift feeling shorter than expected doesn't inform whether everyone helped pack up afterward.
